```{r setup}
library(vgplotr)
```

Every graphic vgplotr renders is ultimately a response to a live SQL 
query against a DuckDB database -- that's what makes Mosaic's 
graphics interactive and scalable.
By default that database is DuckDB-Wasm,
a real DuckDB compiled to WebAssembly and run entirely inside the browser.
See the *Getting Started* vignette (`vignette("getting-started")`) for
the basics of creating Mosaic graphics. `vg_data()` (including its
`file =`/`query =` forms) and `sql()`/`agg()` (for raw SQL expressions)
all work the same way regardless of which database is actually
running underneath. So it makes sense to begin using the default
DuckDB-Wasm database.

This article is about the *other* option:
rendering against a native DuckDB process instead.

## What you need installed

Native DuckDB rendering needs the `duckdb` and `nanoarrow` packages
(`install.packages(c("duckdb", "nanoarrow"))`); neither is required for
the default DuckDB-Wasm path, so plain `vg_widget(spec)` never needs them.
`vg_info()` reports whether they're installed (and which versions), along
with which Mosaic/DuckDB-Wasm versions this vgplotr bundles for the
default path:

```r
vg_info()
```

## Why you'd want native DuckDB instead of DuckDB-Wasm

DuckDB-Wasm keeps a rendered graphic fully self-contained and shareable as
plain HTML, which is why it's vgplotr's default. But it's still DuckDB
running inside a browser sandbox, which caps how much data it can
comfortably hold and how far it can reach: it can't run DuckDB's own
federation extensions -- `postgres_scanner`/`ATTACH ... (TYPE postgres)`,
`mysql_scanner`, `sqlite_scanner` -- that let a *native* DuckDB process
transparently query Postgres, MySQL, or SQLite as if they were ordinary
local tables. If your data is too large for the browser, or already
in a DuckDB database, or in one of those other databases,
native DuckDB is the way to reach it.

## Connecting to native DuckDB 

### `connector = vg_duckdb_connector(...)`

`vg_widget()` and `vg_render()` accept a `connector =` argument: the default
is `vg_wasm_connector()` (DuckDB-Wasm, as above); `vg_duckdb_connector()`
switches to native DuckDB instead. DuckDB itself has no client-server
network protocol -- it's embedded, not a server you connect to -- so what
this actually does is start a small local HTTP bridge (always on your own
machine, always `127.0.0.1`) that the browser talks to; that part is the
same every time. What varies is what's *behind* the bridge: by default, a
private, in-process DuckDB connection vgplotr creates for you; or a
connection you build yourself, which can reach a hosted DuckDB
service (like [MotherDuck](https://motherduck.com)), another database via DuckDB's federation extensions, or both.

### The default: a private, local connection

```r
# vgplotr creates and manages its own private native DuckDB connection
big_data |> vg_mark_dot(x = ~a, y = ~b) |> vg_render(connector = vg_duckdb_connector())
```

Everything else about building a spec -- `vg_data()`, `vg_mark_*()`,
`vg_interactor()`, transforms, `sql()`/`agg()` -- works exactly the same
way; only how the resulting SQL actually gets executed changes.

### Bringing your own connection (e.g., MotherDuck)

`vg_duckdb_connector()` can also take a connection you build yourself with
the `DBI` and `duckdb` R packages -- including one that reaches
[MotherDuck](https://motherduck.com), a hosted DuckDB service:

```r
# recommended: token via environment variable, nothing else to configure
Sys.setenv(motherduck_token = "...")
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), ":memory:")
DBI::dbExecute(con, "INSTALL motherduck; LOAD motherduck;")
DBI::dbExecute(con, "ATTACH 'md:my_db'")   # picks up motherduck_token from the env

spec |> vg_render(connector = vg_duckdb_connector(con))
```

(The `motherduck` package's `connect_to_motherduck()` wraps this same
`INSTALL`/`LOAD`/`ATTACH` setup, if you'd rather not write it out by hand.)

Because every Mosaic interaction (a brush, a filter, etc.) is a separate
query, round-tripping to a cloud database rather than a local one may feel
less snappy than a purely local native DuckDB connection, which doesn't
incur that latency.

### Using other databases

Since DuckDB's federation extensions are just ordinary SQL, vgplotr
doesn't need any special code to support them -- set up a connection
however you'd normally use DuckDB from R, and hand it to
`vg_duckdb_connector()`:

```r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
DBI::dbExecute(
  con, 
  "INSTALL postgres; LOAD postgres; ATTACH 'dbname=mydb host=...' AS pg (TYPE postgres)"
)

vg_create() |>
  vg_data(name = "orders", query = "SELECT * FROM pg.orders") |>
  vg_mark_dot(data_from = "orders", x = ~date, y = ~amount) |>
  vg_render(connector = vg_duckdb_connector(con))
```

`vg_data(query = ...)` is the same option used for any SQL-defined data
source (see `vignette("getting-started")`) -- here it just happens to
query a table that DuckDB is transparently proxying to Postgres.

### One connection at a time

A connection you supply yourself is never closed by vgplotr;
you own its lifecycle.
Only one native connection is served per R session -- if you need to
switch to a different connection, call `vg_duckdb_server_stop()` first.

### Setting a session default

Since only one native connection is served per session anyway, working
with one for a whole script or analysis usually means passing the same
`connector = vg_duckdb_connector(con)` to every `vg_widget()`/`vg_render()`
call. `vg_set_default_connector()` sets it once instead:

```r
vg_set_default_connector(vg_duckdb_connector(con))

# every subsequent call uses `con` automatically
spec1 |> vg_render()
spec2 |> vg_render()

# a specific call can still override the session default
spec3 |> vg_render(connector = vg_wasm_connector())

vg_set_default_connector()  # back to vg_wasm_connector()
```

## Sharing and security

This article's examples aren't demonstrated live, because native-DuckDB
output behaves differently from DuckDB-Wasm output in one important way:
**it's only interactive on the machine/session that rendered it.** The
browser talks to a server started for that R session; opening
the rendered page again later, or on another machine, gives a graphic that
can't connect to anything. DuckDB-Wasm output has no such limitation --
it's genuinely self-contained -- which is exactly why it stays vgplotr's
default.

The local server also has no authentication: it runs whatever SQL the
page sends it (Mosaic's own generated queries, in normal use), mitigated
by binding to `127.0.0.1` only, never a public network interface. Don't
point `vg_duckdb_connector()` at a connection with more access than you'd
want a browser tab to have -- prefer a read-only role or connection when
attaching to a real external database. See `?vg_duckdb_connector` and
`?vg_duckdb_server_stop` for the full details.
